digest.key_takeaway:
What happens when AI agents can retain months of research, modify their own instructions, learn from failed attempts and build upon new scientific breakthroughs?

At TinyHumans AI, alongside Living Brain, we've been exploring exactly that.

Within three days of a reported proof of the Riemann Hypothesis being released in Lean, our agents produced 17 formal mathematical results involving six named conjectures, some dating back more than 100 years.

But the most interesting part isn't necessarily the mathematics.

It's the architecture that made it possible.

articles.title: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 Aims to Make Robots Safer, More Dexterous, and Faster Learners
articles.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to improve robots' dexterity, reliability, and learning speed, while enabling safer operation in unstructured real-world environments. By Sergio De Simone

articles.title: What the TokenCap MCP Server Gives Your Agent
articles.summary:
TokenCap runs as a local MCP server over stdio. Your editor or agent host starts tokencap serve --mcp, and the agent can ask for ranked files, dependencies, impact and repository rules instead of rediscovering the codebase every session. Nothing leaves the machine: no upload, no LLM call, no API key.

This post covers how that flow behaves on first contact and in daily use, including the parts that used to break.

articles.title: When should you compare two AI agent versions side by side instead of scoring one output?
articles.summary:
Compare two agent versions side by side when quality is subjective, such as tone, helpfulness or style. Score a single output when the check is objective, such as faithfulness to a source or a policy rule. In both cases, swap the order of answers, because LLM judges can favor a position.

articles.summary: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.

articles.summary:
Now that code ships faster than ever, you have more time to spend on projects just for the fun of it. Here's what we can learn through that process as developers.

articles.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
articles.summary: AWS has raised the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions, with no opt-in and no new pricing. The limit had stood since 2018. AWS's post lists the costs: twice the concurrency at the same request rate, three-hour SQS visibility timeouts, and Kafka mappings that must be recreated. Practitioners welcome it and ask what belongs elsewhere. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

articles.title: Building Reliable AI Agents with LangGraph: Human Approval Before Tool Execution
articles.summary:
An AI agent can summarize documents, search databases, and generate reports. Those are relatively safe operations.

But what happens when you give it permission to perform actions?

Imagine an AI agent responsible for managing customer accounts.

A user asks:


Find all inactive customer accounts and disable them.


The agent searches the database, identifies inactive accounts, and prepares an update.

Technically, everything looks correct.

articles.title: 401 Unauthorized? Your API key probably never reached the app
articles.summary:
The error:



401 Unauthorized — Incorrect API key provided






Your first instinct is to regenerate the key. Don't — yet. Nine times out of ten the key itself is fine. The app just never saw it.


  
  
  Why it happens



The variable name in your .env doesn't match what the code looks for — OPENAI_API_KEY vs NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY is a classic.
You edited .env but never restarted the dev server. Env files load once, at startup.
The .env file is in the wrong folder. It belongs in the project root.

Open .env and compare the variable name character for cha

articles.summary:
Automotive customer service has become more complex than it was five years ago. articles.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
articles.summary: Rust 1.100.0, released 12 November 2026, stabilises the never type (!) after ten years of work and makes Infallible an alias for it. The release also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and gives Cargo an opt-in dependency cooldown setting. Some critics note the allocator design still lacks inline storage support. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
articles.summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.

articles.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
articles.summary: The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.

articles.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
articles.summary: The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.

articles.title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
articles.summary: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart for a reported $7.5 billion is part of its efforts to improve the efficiency of its Trainium chips.

articles.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
articles.summary: OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches. By Eran Stiller

articles.title: How to Plan Retries for Multi-Agent Workflows Before You Write Code
articles.summary:
A Mermaid blueprint, Python dataclasses, and a retryable flag decide when a failed agent tries again and when the task goes to a person.

articles.title: Article: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
articles.summary: Moving GenAI into high-stakes production requires treating non-determinism as an engineering problem. This architectural blueprint shows engineering leaders and architects how to build trustworthy agentic workflows using knowledge graphs, dual-layer eval judges, CI/CD release gates, and regression testing against golden datasets to automate drafting while maintaining zero-hallucination compliance. By Ritesh Modi, Sasidhar Gudala
